Featured project

Temperature data restoration

A production temperature table had stopped updating in September 2025, and the gap went unnoticed for seven months. My part: I found the cause, restored the data, and delivered the compliance numbers leadership had requested.

Incident recovery · AWS Glue · Redshift

Restoring a temperature table that stopped updating — 1.6B+ rows recovered.

A food-safety compliance request from leadership showed that a production temperature table had no data after September 2025. I traced the cause to an AWS Glue crawler that had stopped running, restored the data, and put the crawler on a daily schedule.

The request

Temperature table missing seven months of data

Leadership requested food-safety compliance numbers. The production temperature table had no data after September 2025 — seven months of sensor data were missing.

The cause

A stopped crawler

I traced the pipeline end to end and found that an AWS Glue crawler had stopped running. Nothing downstream had raised an alarm.

The fix

Crawler re-run the same night

I re-ran the crawler that night, restoring 1.6B+ rows for December 2025 alone. Compliance numbers for ~71 sites went to leadership the same evening.

Prevention

Crawler put on a daily schedule

The crawler now runs daily, so a stoppage would show up within a day instead of going unnoticed for months.

The gap, Sep 2025 – Apr 2026

Temperature data present by month — the flatline is the silent failure; April is the restored, daily-running pipeline.

Analytics & BIAmazon

HVAC End-of-Life Asset Intelligence

Equipment lifecycle dataset for replacement planning. One asset register merged from three data sources (22,305, 19,761 and 11,530 records). Asset age was derived from serial numbers where no source system records a manufacture date.

$2.76Bin reported spend corrected by fixing a many-to-many join defect

My slice: Built the merged asset register — the deduplication, source-prioritization and serial-number age-decoding logic are mine; the 48,980 assets are the program's fleet.

Read more

53,596 records were merged into 48,980 deduplicated assets across 4,402 sites. Per-site source-prioritization logic was used to prevent double-counting. Asset age was derived from serial numbers using decode logic for 30+ manufacturers, because neither source holds a reliable manufacture date. Contested sites were verified individually. A many-to-many join defect that had inflated reported spend was fixed, correcting $2.76B.

SQLQuickSightPythonData quality

EV Charger Operations — Vendor SLA Measurement

Vendor performance, support-tier and power-cycle analytics for EV charger operations in Europe and North America. Built on approximately 95 engineered fields.

191K → 3.4Mrows after redesigning the dataset so open work orders report every open day

My slice: Found the mis-anchored SLA timestamp and rebuilt the measurement on audit events, including the row-per-open-day redesign; charger operations themselves are the vendor's.

Read more

The vendor-dispatch timestamp is the anchor for the SLA metrics. It was keyed to a proxy field. The timestamp was re-anchored to the actual dispatch event and measurement was rebuilt on audit events. The dataset was redesigned so that an open work order generates one row for each day it is open. The date dimension increased from 191K rows to 3.4M rows. The redesigned dataset is used for lifecycle, aging and trend reporting.

Data EngineeringAmazon

Pipeline Reliability — Silent Failures & a 91% Runtime Cut

Production dashboard refreshes were being cancelled by a cluster-wide scan limit. Dashboards showed stale data and no error was displayed. The affected queries were optimized.

170 → 15 mincompliance aggregation runtime — a 91% reduction

My slice: Diagnosed the silent scan-limit cancellations and rewrote the affected queries; the cluster and its limits are platform-owned.

Read more

The affected queries were optimized using date floors, region scoping and deduplication fixes. After optimization, refreshes completed in minutes. A compliance aggregation job was moved out of a contended schedule window. Its runtime fell from 170 minutes to 15 minutes.

RedshiftSQLGlueQuery optimization
